value.text: Four travellers must cross a bridge at night with one torch. At most two cross at a time and a pair moves at the slower person's pace. They take 1, 2, 5 and 10 minutes. What is the fastest total crossing time, and what is the schedule?

**The fastest total is 17 minutes.**

| Step | Move | Time | Elapsed |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1 and 2 cross together | 2 | 2 |
| 2 | 1 returns with the torch | 1 | 3 |
| 3 | 5 and 10 cross together | 10 | 13 |
| 4 | 2 returns with the torch | 2 | 15 |
| 5 | 1 and 2 cross together | 2 | 17 |

**Why this is best:** The two slowest travellers (5 and 10) should cross together, so the 5-minute person's time is absorbed into the 10-minute crossing. The 1 and 2 travellers are already on the far side after step 1. One of them can bring the torch back, so neither the 5 nor the 10 has to walk back.

The obvious alternative, where the 1-minute person escorts everyone, costs 2 + 1 + 5 + 1 + 10 = 19 minutes. If 5 and 10 cross separately, the two slow trips alone cost 15, plus at least 2 for the return trips and 2 for the last forward trip, giving at least 19. Crossing together is the only way to get below 19, and 17 is the best such schedule.
